analysis.title: Microsoft Corporation: A closer look at Copilot: a conversation with Copilot EVP, Jacob Andreou
key_insights: BofA reiterates Buy on MSFT with a $630 price objective versus a $498.30 price, after an investor meeting with Copilot EVP Jacob Andreou.
Microsoft frames enterprise AI around model flexibility, predictable costs and business context from the M365 ecosystem, which BofA says supports paid Copilot seat expansion plus consumption pricing.

Copilot users are split into three groups: Starters (limited Copilot included in existing M365 plans), Subscribers (paid seat) and Advanced users (pay for AI consumption via modules like Autopilot and Code).
With paid subscribers on a healthier trajectory, management is shifting attention to converting Starters into paid seats and driving consumption revenue from Advanced users.
Advanced offerings named include Cowork for analysis across files, Code for custom apps and dashboards, and Autopilot for background tasks.

Work IQ is evolving from file retrieval to a semantic understanding of work across emails, Teams conversations and documents. Andreou argued model intelligence has limited value without business context.

Office network effects are a stated edge against AI labs entering productivity software. Users can adopt Copilot without colleagues changing tools, and Copilot Workspaces provides a shared team space.
Hybrid pricing includes everyday AI in the Copilot subscription while complex workloads are metered. Auto mode mixes cheaper and frontier models within a task to control cost.
Longer term, Microsoft wants proactive assistance (the Today feature) and always-on agents. BofA sees Copilot becoming the central interface for knowledge work across Microsoft and third-party apps.
The price objective rests on 28x CY27E P/E, a premium to the 18-25x peer group. Risks are Azure gross margin pressure, faster AI-lab innovation and cyclical enterprise application spending.

market_movers.rationale: Copilot strategy built on model flexibility, predictable cost and Work IQ business context supports seat and consumption growth. PO based on 28x CY27E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: BofA sees Microsoft's Copilot approach giving enterprises a practical path to AI adoption at scale.

risk_factors: Near-term gross margin pressure as Azure grows as a share of revenue.
AI applications and model providers could innovate faster than Microsoft and limit its growth.
Enterprise application spending is cyclical and discretionary.
Increased competition from AI labs expanding into productivity software.
